purpose: Mandatory target policy, not a recovered release inventory or compatibility certification.
scope: Every publicly released PHP generation from the first public PHP Tools onward, including exact patch identities and separately identified public prereleases.

required_generations.name: First PHP Tools and PHP 1 lineage
special_requirements: Establish first public release identity independently of the php-108 archive.
Recover original tool/CGI behavior and original examples.

required_generations.name: FI, Construction Kit, PHP/FI and PHP/FI 2
special_requirements: Separate historical syntax and tool entrypoints.
Do not force HTML-comment instruction forms into modern PHP syntax.

required_generations.name: PHP 3
special_requirements: Exact releases, module contracts, language and environment semantics.

required_generations.name: PHP 4
special_requirements: Historical object/reference behavior and application fixtures.

required_generations.name: PHP 5
special_requirements: Every released minor/patch identity, not only the final branch.

required_generations.name: PHP 7
special_requirements: Every released minor/patch identity and guest-platform behavior.

required_generations.name: PHP 8
special_requirements: Current and historical releases, dynamic features, exact function behavior.

future_release_rule: Continuously add new public releases with independent source locks and certification; no claim of advance verification.
unreleased_version_rule: Do not invent a formal PHP 6 release. Evidence-backed experimental snapshots are a distinct research category.
missing_evidence_rule: Unresolved release identity, unavailable source, unavailable oracle or missing real application evidence remains a visible blocker, never a pass or implicit scope removal.
